knowledge:
- key_parameters: object=A data frame, matrix, or an object inheriting from eSets (e.g. ExpressionSet, MethylSet) containing raw, unprocessed high-throughput data (probes/genes on rows, samples on columns) ;; groupFactor=A factor or vector representing group-level information for each sample ;; B=The number of permutations to perform for assessing statistical significance (default is 0; set B > 0 to run permutation testing) ;; brewer.n=The number of colors to use from the RColorBrewer palette in matdensity and matboxplot ;; brewer.name=The name of the RColorBrewer palette to use in matdensity and matboxplot ;; xLab=The x-axis label for quantroPlot ;; yLab=The y-axis label for quantroPlot ;; mainLab=The title of the histogram in quantroPlot ;; binWidth=The binwidth of the histogram in quantroPlot
- alternatives: Global normalization methods (such as quantile normalization) are the standard alternative; they should be preferred only if the quantro test fails to reject the null hypothesis (i.e., when there are no global differences in distributions between biological groups).
- when_to_use: Use this analysis on raw, unprocessed high-throughput data (e.g., microarrays, DNA methylation, RNA-Seq, ChIP-Seq) before normalization to test if the statistical distributions of the biological groups differ globally. It is especially appropriate when a biological group is expected to have a substantially different proportion of active features (e.g., genes or methylation sites), where global normalization would incorrectly wipe out real biological differences.
- pitfalls: Applying global normalization when the assumptions are violated can wipe out biologically interesting global changes and artificially induce false differences in features that are not actually different. Failing to register a parallel backend (e.g., using doParallel) when running a large number of permutations (B) can result in extremely slow computation times. The test must be performed on raw, unprocessed data, not on already normalized data.

workflows.name: quantro_normalization_test
workflows.intent: Test for global differences in distributions between sample groups to determine if global normalization is appropriate.
input: raw_data.matrix (matrix or data frame of raw high-throughput measurements)
sample_metadata.csv (phenotypic data containing group-level factors for each sample)
workflows.stages: 1. Visualize raw sample distributions using matdensity and matboxplot ;; 2. Run the main quantro test to calculate the test statistic and perform ANOVA on medians ;; 3. Perform permutation testing with a registered parallel backend to assess statistical significance ;; 4. Plot the permutation test results using quantroPlot
workflows.code:
matdensity(p, groupFactor = pd$CellType, xlab = " ", ylab = "density",
           main = "Beta Values", brewer.n = 8, brewer.name = "Dark2")
legend('top', c("NeuN_neg", "NeuN_pos"), col = c(1, 2), lty = 1, lwd = 3)
matboxplot(p, groupFactor = pd$CellType, xaxt = "n", main = "Beta Values")
qtest <- quantro(object = p, groupFactor = pd$CellType)
qtest
summary(qtest)
anova(qtest)
quantroStat(qtest)
qtest <- quantro(flowSorted, groupFactor = pData(flowSorted)$CellType)
qtest 
library(doParallel)
registerDoParallel(cores=1)
qtestPerm <- quantro(p, groupFactor = pd$CellType, B = 1000)
qtestPerm
quantroPlot(qtestPerm)
